# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **AI Collaboration Rule**:
> - **Planning**, **Brainstorming**, **Implementation** and **Bug fixes** are all
>   in scope. Planning is no longer delegated to Gemini (Antigravity).
> - Implementation plans go in `.claude/plans/` (see
>   [rules/planning.md](rules/planning.md)); design decisions that outlive a plan
>   are recorded in `docs/backlog.md`. Open work (stories, tasks, bugs) is tracked
>   in Plane, see the `## Plane` section of the root `CLAUDE.md`.
> - Always refer to [project-context.md](../project-context.md) for global project rules.
>   It sits in this repository, at the root. The absolute path this line used to
>   carry named a GitLab checkout that is no longer where DevDesk lives.

## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP) + real-time port monitoring + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only) + a path trace under Diagnostics (Trace Path button, or `H` on the route row; no separate tab since DEVDESK-471) (native path trace, on native Linux, native Windows (IPv4 only, ICMP echoes through `iphlpapi`, DEVDESK-486) and WSL2: on macOS and WSL1 the button, `H`, `enter` and `ctrl+o` are greyed and the footer says why, DEVDESK-334; the column starts with this machine, its interface and its gateway; `ctrl+o` can start it from a running Docker Engine container instead (container and network rows, hops still traced from this machine); `H` on the Diagnostics route row opens the trace level on that host without starting it (greyed with the reason on an unsupported platform or a target the trace refuses; its interface and gateway rows reuse the Local route check's reading of the same address, read once, DEVDESK-473), and in the trace level `enter` starts or restarts it, `ctrl+o` picks the source, `esc` cancels then goes back where it came from; under WSL2 the source row says `WSL2 (VM), not the Windows host` with the networking mode, and in NAT mode the gateway and TTL 1 hop are tagged `Windows host (virtual switch)` only when proven, DEVDESK-333; the interface row says `no route` when the kernel proves there is none and `undetermined` when the routing table could not be read, a no-route error keeps the local rows, a trace that ends on the hop limit or the deadline folds its silent tail into one `silent` row and marks the `last to answer` hop, and the target refuses a `:port`, DEVDESK-335)
- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
- Local workspaces management with git metadata
- Claude Code session list (`:agent-usage` / `:au`): sessions found on this machine, by project and date, and per session the agent tree (orchestrator and sub-agents: types, models, tokens, share of the total; sortable by Total; also per agent a state (running / idle / done / unknown, idle after 5 min without a transcript line) shown as a status dot in the first column (the `running` dot blinks, DEVDESK-151) and as text, tool calls and duration; and an indicative cost per agent, `Est. cost` (orange from 75 % and red from 90 % of the session's estimated cost, when at least two agents are priced), from prices you write in the context YAML (`agent_usage.prices`, none shipped), with the session's `Billed` cost and `Unattributed` in the header, DEVDESK-47; a `Breakdown` colour bar per agent and, with `tab` inside a session, a Breakdown tab splitting the whole session's tokens by category, model and agent, as a percentage of tokens, DEVDESK-98). An open session updates live: read again every 2 s while active, only what was appended; paused after 5 min with no write and no unfinished sub-agent, when its transcript is gone, or while the terminal is not focused (header `Updates › paused`, then `paused (terminal not focused)`; `app.when_unfocused: run` keeps it live); `ctrl+r` reads it again in full. The sessions list itself is not live.

## Build and Development Commands

Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.

```bash
# Development (fastest)
mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
go run .

# Build
mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
```

### Status Monitoring System

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

### Component CRUD Operations

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog
- Changes persist to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` via `config.Save()`

State flags in Model: `creating`, `editing`, `confirming`, `selectedIdx`

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

## Testing

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

Use table-driven tests where appropriate.

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
  enforces it yet.

**Nexus tests replay recorded fixtures (DEVDESK-511).** The tests of the Nexus
code (`internal/imagesearch`, `internal/registrymgr`) replay answers measured on
the bench from `internal/nexusfixture/fixtures/`, through
`internal/nexusfixture/fakenexus`: `mise run test` needs no bench, no cluster and
no secret. Every fixture is leak-checked in the suite; set
`DEVDESK_FIXTURE_DENYLIST` to a file kept outside the repository (one term per
line) to add names the repository must not carry. A fixture whose Nexus version
differs from `internal/nexusbench/descriptor.json` fails the suite: regenerate
with `mise run nexus-bench:record`. See `docs/architecture/nexus-bench.md`.

**Test input and colour (DEVDESK-199).** Build keys only through
`internal/ui/testutil` (`Key`, `Keys`, `Type`, `Paste`, `Text`, `IsText`), never a
literal `tea.KeyPressMsg` or `tea.Key*`. `Key` returns a
`tea.KeyPressMsg` (`Keys` and `Type` return a message list), `Paste` a `tea.PasteMsg`; `Key` is strict: an unknown name
panics. The space key is built as a key (`Key("space")`), never matched through
`String()` (v1 `" "`, v2 `"space"`). Lip Gloss v2 has no global colour profile (`Style.Render` always emits full
colour), so a test needs no setup to check styling; it reads the SGR or strips it
with `ansi.Strip`. `internal/ui/testutil/source_guard_test.go` fails the suite on a
hand-built key, a `colorprofile` import outside `internal/app/profile_test.go` and
`internal/app/redraw_measure_test.go` or `SetColorProfile` in any `_test.go`. Paste tests
(`internal/app/paste_test.go`, `wrapped_input_test.go`, `component_form_test.go`):
a paste reaches the focused field, newlines become spaces in single-line fields,
and no key action fires (Rule 111).

**Space and key API (DEVDESK-200).** Production code matches the space key as
`keymap.Space`, never `" "`/`"space"`, and reads keys through `String()` only
(no `.Runes`, `.Alt`, `.Paste`, `tea.KeyType` or `tea.Key<Name>`). Update
handlers switch on `tea.KeyPressMsg`, never the `tea.KeyMsg` interface (it also
matches releases). A paste is a `tea.PasteMsg`, not a key (Rule 111). Guards in
`internal/ui/keymap` (`space_scan_test.go`, `legacy_key_scan_test.go`,
`viewport_keymap_scan_test.go`) fail the suite otherwise; limits are listed in
`docs/architecture/app-shell.md`.

- `charm.land/bubbletea/v2` (v2.1.1) - TUI framework (v2: `tea.KeyPressMsg`, `tea.PasteMsg`, `View() tea.View`)
- `charm.land/bubbles/v2` (v2.2.1) - Pre-built TUI components (table, textinput, viewport)
- `charm.land/lipgloss/v2` (v2.0.6) - Styling (no global colour profile; colours are `image/color.Color`)
- `github.com/charmbracelet/colorprofile` (v0.4.3) - colour profile `main.go` forces under Windows Terminal (replaces `termenv`)
- `github.com/NimbleMarkets/ntcharts/v2` (v2.9.0) - dashboard sparkline
- `github.com/charmbracelet/x/ansi` - ANSI-safe width, strip and cut
- `gitlab.com/gitlab-org/api/client-go` - GitLab API client
- `github.com/prometheus-community/pro-bing` - ICMP ping functionality (maintained fork of go-ping/ping)
- `github.com/google/go-github/v68` - GitHub API client (§3.6)
- `github.com/libp2p/go-netroute` - which interface a destination leaves by, on all three platforms (§3.44)
- `golang.org/x/sys` - direct (Rule 303): the socket calls of `internal/nettrace` (`IP_TTL`, `IP_RECVERR`, `recvmsg` on the error queue); `x/sys/windows` serves `iphlpapi` (the Windows path trace, `IcmpSendEcho2`)
- `github.com/zalando/go-keyring` - host secret manager (wincred / Keychain / Secret Service), no cgo
- `gopkg.in/yaml.v3` - YAML configuration

## Code Conventions

- Comments: **English only** (Rule 307) — existing French comments are not rewritten wholesale, but any new or edited comment is in English
- Commit messages: **English only** (Rule 307)
- UI text and logs: **English US only** (Rule 129)
- Bubbletea models define their own message types
- Use `theme` package for consistent styling (`internal/ui/theme/`)
- Config changes must call `config.Save()` to persist
- All colors defined in `theme/colors.go`, all styles in `theme/styles.go`
- Message naming: `[ComponentName][Action]Msg` (e.g., `ComponentFormSubmitMsg`)
- Context names: the rule exists twice (`config.ValidateContextName`, `contextcmd.ValidName`); change both or neither (`TestContextNameRulesAgree`). Creation refuses `-`, `new`, `list` (`config.ValidateNewContextName`); loading does not (D91)

## Critical Bubble Tea Rules

**NEVER modify model state inside a Cmd** (Rule 110) - Race condition:
- `Update()` is the ONLY place to modify model state
- `View()` is read-only
- `Cmd` functions do I/O and return messages

**NEVER use `style.Render()` inside `table.Row{}`** (Rule 122) - ANSI sequences corrupt all subsequent rows:
- Use plain text: `theme.IconError + " error"` not `theme.StatusErrorStyle.Render(...)`
- Apply row styling via `table.SetStyles(theme.TableStylesForState("error"))`

**Views render through `Render()`** (Bubble Tea v2): a top-level view implements
`Render() string` and `View() tea.View { return tea.NewView(m.Render()) }`; only the
router (`App.View()`) sets terminal state such as `AltScreen` and `BackgroundColor`. Components keep
`View() string`. Colours are `color.Color`; hex literals stay in `theme/colors.go`.

**Update() case extraction**: If a case block exceeds 5 lines, extract to `handle[MessageType]()` method returning `(tea.Model, tea.Cmd)`

- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

**Parallel Execution:**

- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog

State flags in Model: `creating`, `editing`, `confirming`, `selectedIdx`

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

Use table-driven tests where appropriate.

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
  enforces it yet.

code (`internal/imagesearch`, `internal/registrymgr`) replay answers measured on
the bench from `internal/nexusfixture/fixtures/`, through
`internal/nexusfixture/fakenexus`: `mise run test` needs no bench, no cluster and
no secret. Every fixture is leak-checked in the suite; set
`DEVDESK_FIXTURE_DENYLIST` to a file kept outside the repository (one term per
line) to add names the repository must not carry. A fixture whose Nexus version
differs from `internal/nexusbench/descriptor.json` fails the suite: regenerate
with `mise run nexus-bench:record`. See `docs/architecture/nexus-bench.md`.

**Test input and colour (DEVDESK-199).** Build keys only through
`internal/ui/testutil` (`Key`, `Keys`, `Type`, `Paste`, `Text`, `IsText`), never a
literal `tea.KeyPressMsg` or `tea.Key*`. `Key` returns a
`tea.KeyPressMsg` (`Keys` and `Type` return a message list), `Paste` a `tea.PasteMsg`; `Key` is strict: an unknown name
panics. The space key is built as a key (`Key("space")`), never matched through
`String()` (v1 `" "`, v2 `"space"`). Lip Gloss v2 has no global colour profile (`Style.Render` always emits full
colour), so a test needs no setup to check styling; it reads the SGR or strips it
with `ansi.Strip`. `internal/ui/testutil/source_guard_test.go` fails the suite on a
hand-built key, a `colorprofile` import outside `internal/app/profile_test.go` and
`internal/app/redraw_measure_test.go` or `SetColorProfile` in any `_test.go`. Paste tests
(`internal/app/paste_test.go`, `wrapped_input_test.go`, `component_form_test.go`):
a paste reaches the focused field, newlines become spaces in single-line fields,
and no key action fires (Rule 111).

**Space and key API (DEVDESK-200).** Production code matches the space key as
`keymap.Space`, never `" "`/`"space"`, and reads keys through `String()` only
(no `.Runes`, `.Alt`, `.Paste`, `tea.KeyType` or `tea.Key<Name>`). Update
handlers switch on `tea.KeyPressMsg`, never the `tea.KeyMsg` interface (it also
matches releases). A paste is a `tea.PasteMsg`, not a key (Rule 111). Guards in
`internal/ui/keymap` (`space_scan_test.go`, `legacy_key_scan_test.go`,
`viewport_keymap_scan_test.go`) fail the suite otherwise; limits are listed in
`docs/architecture/app-shell.md`.

## Dependencies

Go 1.27 (`go 1.27.3` in `go.mod`). Key libraries (versions as in `go.mod`):
- `charm.land/bubbletea/v2` (v2.1.1) - TUI framework (v2: `tea.KeyPressMsg`, `tea.PasteMsg`, `View() tea.View`)
- `charm.land/bubbles/v2` (v2.2.1) - Pre-built TUI components (table, textinput, viewport)
- `charm.land/lipgloss/v2` (v2.0.6) - Styling (no global colour profile; colours are `image/color.Color`)
- `github.com/charmbracelet/colorprofile` (v0.4.3) - colour profile `main.go` forces under Windows Terminal (replaces `termenv`)
- `github.com/NimbleMarkets/ntcharts/v2` (v2.9.0) - dashboard sparkline
- `github.com/charmbracelet/x/ansi` - ANSI-safe width, strip and cut
- `gitlab.com/gitlab-org/api/client-go` - GitLab API client
- `github.com/prometheus-community/pro-bing` - ICMP ping functionality (maintained fork of go-ping/ping)
- `github.com/google/go-github/v68` - GitHub API client (§3.6)
- `github.com/libp2p/go-netroute` - which interface a destination leaves by, on all three platforms (§3.44)

- `github.com/zalando/go-keyring` - host secret manager (wincred / Keychain / Secret Service), no cgo
- `gopkg.in/yaml.v3` - YAML configuration

## Code Conventions

- Comments: **English only** (Rule 307) — existing French comments are not rewritten wholesale, but any new or edited comment is in English
- Commit messages: **English only** (Rule 307)
- UI text and logs: **English US only** (Rule 129)
- Bubbletea models define their own message types
- Use `theme` package for consistent styling (`internal/ui/theme/`)
- Config changes must call `config.Save()` to persist
- All colors defined in `theme/colors.go`, all styles in `theme/styles.go`
- Message naming: `[ComponentName][Action]Msg` (e.g., `ComponentFormSubmitMsg`)
- Context names: the rule exists twice (`config.ValidateContextName`, `contextcmd.ValidName`); change both or neither (`TestContextNameRulesAgree`). Creation refuses `-`, `new`, `list` (`config.ValidateNewContextName`); loading does not (D91)

## Critical Bubble Tea Rules

**NEVER modify model state inside a Cmd** (Rule 110) - Race condition:
- `Update()` is the ONLY place to modify model state
- `View()` is read-only
- `Cmd` functions do I/O and return messages

**NEVER use `style.Render()` inside `table.Row{}`** (Rule 122) - ANSI sequences corrupt all subsequent rows:
- Use plain text: `theme.IconError + " error"` not `theme.StatusErrorStyle.Render(...)`
- Apply row styling via `table.SetStyles(theme.TableStylesForState("error"))`

**Views render through `Render()`** (Bubble Tea v2): a top-level view implements
`Render() string` and `View() tea.View { return tea.NewView(m.Render()) }`; only the
router (`App.View()`) sets terminal state such as `AltScreen` and `BackgroundColor`. Components keep
`View() string`. Colours are `color.Color`; hex literals stay in `theme/colors.go`.

**Update() case extraction**: If a case block exceeds 5 lines, extract to `handle[MessageType]()` method returning `(tea.Model, tea.Cmd)`

The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

## Testing

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

Use table-driven tests where appropriate.

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
  enforces it yet.

**Nexus tests replay recorded fixtures (DEVDESK-511).** The tests of the Nexus
code (`internal/imagesearch`, `internal/registrymgr`) replay answers measured on
the bench from `internal/nexusfixture/fixtures/`, through
`internal/nexusfixture/fakenexus`: `mise run test` needs no bench, no cluster and
no secret. Every fixture is leak-checked in the suite; set
`DEVDESK_FIXTURE_DENYLIST` to a file kept outside the repository (one term per
line) to add names the repository must not carry. A fixture whose Nexus version
differs from `internal/nexusbench/descriptor.json` fails the suite: regenerate
with `mise run nexus-bench:record`. See `docs/architecture/nexus-bench.md`.

**Test input and colour (DEVDESK-199).** Build keys only through
`internal/ui/testutil` (`Key`, `Keys`, `Type`, `Paste`, `Text`, `IsText`), never a
literal `tea.KeyPressMsg` or `tea.Key*`. `Key` returns a
`tea.KeyPressMsg` (`Keys` and `Type` return a message list), `Paste` a `tea.PasteMsg`; `Key` is strict: an unknown name
panics. The space key is built as a key (`Key("space")`), never matched through
`String()` (v1 `" "`, v2 `"space"`). Lip Gloss v2 has no global colour profile (`Style.Render` always emits full
colour), so a test needs no setup to check styling; it reads the SGR or strips it
with `ansi.Strip`. `internal/ui/testutil/source_guard_test.go` fails the suite on a
hand-built key, a `colorprofile` import outside `internal/app/profile_test.go` and
`internal/app/redraw_measure_test.go` or `SetColorProfile` in any `_test.go`. Paste tests
(`internal/app/paste_test.go`, `wrapped_input_test.go`, `component_form_test.go`):
a paste reaches the focused field, newlines become spaces in single-line fields,
and no key action fires (Rule 111).

**Space and key API (DEVDESK-200).** Production code matches the space key as
`keymap.Space`, never `" "`/`"space"`, and reads keys through `String()` only
(no `.Runes`, `.Alt`, `.Paste`, `tea.KeyType` or `tea.Key<Name>`). Update
handlers switch on `tea.KeyPressMsg`, never the `tea.KeyMsg` interface (it also
matches releases). A paste is a `tea.PasteMsg`, not a key (Rule 111). Guards in
`internal/ui/keymap` (`space_scan_test.go`, `legacy_key_scan_test.go`,
`viewport_keymap_scan_test.go`) fail the suite otherwise; limits are listed in
`docs/architecture/app-shell.md`.

Go 1.27 (`go 1.27.3` in `go.mod`). Key libraries (versions as in `go.mod`):
- `charm.land/bubbletea/v2` (v2.1.1) - TUI framework (v2: `tea.KeyPressMsg`, `tea.PasteMsg`, `View() tea.View`)
- `charm.land/bubbles/v2` (v2.2.1) - Pre-built TUI components (table, textinput, viewport)
- `charm.land/lipgloss/v2` (v2.0.6) - Styling (no global colour profile; colours are `image/color.Color`)
- `github.com/charmbracelet/colorprofile` (v0.4.3) - colour profile `main.go` forces under Windows Terminal (replaces `termenv`)
- `github.com/NimbleMarkets/ntcharts/v2` (v2.9.0) - dashboard sparkline
- `github.com/charmbracelet/x/ansi` - ANSI-safe width, strip and cut
- `gitlab.com/gitlab-org/api/client-go` - GitLab API client
- `github.com/prometheus-community/pro-bing` - ICMP ping functionality (maintained fork of go-ping/ping)
- `github.com/google/go-github/v68` - GitHub API client (§3.6)

- `github.com/zalando/go-keyring` - host secret manager (wincred / Keychain / Secret Service), no cgo
- `gopkg.in/yaml.v3` - YAML configuration

## Code Conventions

- Comments: **English only** (Rule 307) — existing French comments are not rewritten wholesale, but any new or edited comment is in English
- Commit messages: **English only** (Rule 307)
- UI text and logs: **English US only** (Rule 129)
- Bubbletea models define their own message types
- Use `theme` package for consistent styling (`internal/ui/theme/`)
- Config changes must call `config.Save()` to persist
- All colors defined in `theme/colors.go`, all styles in `theme/styles.go`
- Message naming: `[ComponentName][Action]Msg` (e.g., `ComponentFormSubmitMsg`)
- Context names: the rule exists twice (`config.ValidateContextName`, `contextcmd.ValidName`); change both or neither (`TestContextNameRulesAgree`). Creation refuses `-`, `new`, `list` (`config.ValidateNewContextName`); loading does not (D91)

## Critical Bubble Tea Rules

**NEVER modify model state inside a Cmd** (Rule 110) - Race condition:
- `Update()` is the ONLY place to modify model state
- `View()` is read-only
- `Cmd` functions do I/O and return messages

**NEVER use `style.Render()` inside `table.Row{}`** (Rule 122) - ANSI sequences corrupt all subsequent rows:
- Use plain text: `theme.IconError + " error"` not `theme.StatusErrorStyle.Render(...)`
- Apply row styling via `table.SetStyles(theme.TableStylesForState("error"))`

**Views render through `Render()`** (Bubble Tea v2): a top-level view implements
`Render() string` and `View() tea.View { return tea.NewView(m.Render()) }`; only the
router (`App.View()`) sets terminal state such as `AltScreen` and `BackgroundColor`. Components keep
`View() string`. Colours are `color.Color`; hex literals stay in `theme/colors.go`.

**Update() case extraction**: If a case block exceeds 5 lines, extract to `handle[MessageType]()` method returning `(tea.Model, tea.Cmd)`

  ## Proxy d'environnement (HTTP_PROXY / HTTPS_PROXY / NO_PROXY) dans DevDesk : analyse du code
  
  Analyse faite en lecture seule sur main (9f878a2a). Je n'ai écrit aucun fichier.
  
  ### Réponse courte
  
  **Oui pour presque tous les appels HTTP que DevDesk fait lui-même, mais par défaut, pas par conception.** DevDesk n'a aucun réglage de proxy à lui : pas de clé YAML (`network.proxy_port` est le port du reverse proxy local des forwards, `internal/config/config.go:137`), pas d'option, pas de documentation utilisateur. Seuls `docs/architecture/network.md:173` et `nexus-bench.md` en parlent. Les clients HTTP Go passent tous par `http.DefaultTransport`, ou par un transport qui en dérive, donc par `http.ProxyFromEnvironment`, sauf trois exceptions :
  - `netcheck` (Diagnostics), sans que rien ne le signale ;
  - les forwards, ce qui est voulu ;
  - `nexusbench`, voulu aussi.
  
  Les sous-processus (git, docker/podman, trivy/gitleaks/cosign/plumber installés comme binaires) héritent de l'environnement. En revanche, **les scanners lancés en conteneur ne reçoivent pas les variables de proxy de DevDesk.**
  
  Ce que fait Go (vérifié dans le source de Go 1.27, `vendor/golang.org/x/net/http/httpproxy/proxy.go:92-95, 170-200`) :
  - **Majuscules et minuscules :** `getEnvAny("HTTP_PROXY","http_proxy")`, la forme en majuscules l'emporte si les deux sont posées. Même chose pour HTTPS_PROXY et NO_PROXY. HTTP_PROXY est ignorée si `REQUEST_METHOD` est posée (cas CGI).
  - **Lecture unique :** l'environnement est lu une seule fois par processus (`sync.Once`). Un changement de contexte ne le relit pas.
  - **Hôtes jamais proxifiés :** `localhost` exact et les IP de bouclage littérales. Un nom `*.localhost`, lui, part au proxy.
  - **NO_PROXY :** accepte une liste séparée par des virgules, des noms, des suffixes (`.example.com` ou `example.com`, qui couvre aussi les sous-domaines), `*`, des IP, des CIDR et `hôte:port`. Un CIDR ne s'applique qu'à une IP littérale dans l'URL, jamais à un nom résolu.
  - **Schémas de proxy :** `http`, `https`, `socks5` et `socks5h` (`net/http/transport.go:1940`), avec authentification Basic par l'userinfo de l'URL. Pas de NTLM ni de Kerberos, d'où l'usage de cntlm cité dans le code.
  - **ALL_PROXY / all_proxy : ignorées par tous les clients Go.** Un SOCKS ne marche que si on le met dans HTTP(S)_PROXY. git (libcurl) lit, lui, `all_proxy`.

  | `imagesearch` Hub | oui | client par défaut, `HubSearcher{}` | `internal/imagesearch/hub.go:71-79`, `internal/ui/oci_resources/browser_flow.go:70` |
  | `imagesearch` catalog | oui | `oci.ListCatalogContext` | `internal/imagesearch/catalog.go:43` |
  | Dates des tags Docker Hub (navigateur de registres) | oui | DefaultTransport | `internal/ui/oci_resources/commands.go:362` |
  | `registrymgr` (API REST Nexus) | oui | DefaultTransport | `internal/registrymgr/nexus.go:48` |
  | `status` HTTP/HTTPS | oui | DefaultTransport | `internal/status/http_checker.go:19-30` |

  | `status` DNS / ICMP | non applicable | résolveur Go / pro-bing | `internal/status/dns_checker.go:49-52`, `internal/status/icmp_checker.go:42` |

  | **`netcheck` HTTP HEAD** | **non** : `&http.Transport{TLSClientConfig: …}` sans champ `Proxy`, donc aucun proxy | Transport explicite | `internal/netcheck/env.go:305-315` |
  | Forwards (TCP et routes HTTP nommées) | non, voulu (reverse proxy local vers la cible) | `routeTransport` sans `Proxy`, `net.DialTimeout` | `internal/forward/proxy.go:468-472`, `internal/forward/forward.go:558` |

- **Fonctionnement :** `dialControl` (`internal/oci/oci_blob.go:75-90`) refuse à la connexion une adresse de bouclage, link-local ou non spécifiée. Seule exception : l'ip:port d'un proxy que la fonction `Proxy` a choisi pour une requête. `proxyAddrs.add` le résout une fois et le garde (`oci_blob.go:122-147`, port par défaut selon le schéma : 80, 443, 1080 pour socks5 et socks5h). Un proxy local comme cntlm sur 127.0.0.1 continue donc de marcher.
- **Une cible exclue par NO_PROXY :** `Proxy()` renvoie nil et ne déclare rien. La connexion est directe et la garde s'applique sur l'IP résolue.
- **Risque résiduel accepté (4) de D156 :** une fois un proxy vu, son ip:port reste autorisé pour toute connexion du transport. Un nom exclu par NO_PROXY qui résout vers cet ip:port passe donc en direct (GET anonyme).
- **Risque résiduel (3) :** derrière un proxy, c'est le proxy qui résout la cible, donc seule la vérification du nom littéral (`followBlobRedirect`) protège.
- **Seul composant testé avec un proxy :** `internal/oci/oci_blob_proxy_test.go`, avec un proxy injecté par `newBlobTransport` puisque `ProxyFromEnvironment` est figé par processus.

1. **Les Diagnostics contournent le proxy sans le dire.** Le HEAD HTTP a un Transport explicite sans `Proxy` (`internal/netcheck/env.go:306`). Le stage HTTP dépend en plus du stage connect, qui est une connexion TCP directe (`internal/netcheck/stage_http.go:22-30`). Derrière un proxy obligatoire, l'écran conclut « injoignable » alors que tous les autres clients de DevDesk passent par le proxy. Aucune ligne n'indique qu'un proxy est configuré pour cette cible ni que NO_PROXY l'exclut. Un diagnostic direct peut être voulu, mais rien dans le code ni dans la doc ne le dit.
2. **Les moniteurs de statut divergent.** Un moniteur `http`/`https` passe par le proxy, un moniteur `ssl` sur la même cible part en direct (`internal/status/tls_dial.go:27`). L'un peut être vert et l'autre en erreur pour le même hôte.

   - la CLI Docker injecte les proxys de `~/.docker/config.json` (`proxies`), pas ceux de l'environnement ;
   - podman transmet par défaut les variables de l'hôte (`--http-proxy=true`) ;
   - dans les deux cas, un proxy sur 127.0.0.1 n'est pas joignable depuis un conteneur en réseau bridge.

   DevDesk donne donc un résultat différent selon le moteur et la source de l'outil (binaire ou conteneur).
4. **La sémantique change entre Go et git.** libcurl ignore `HTTP_PROXY` en majuscules pour les URL `http://` (protection httpoxy) et lit `all_proxy`. Go lit `HTTP_PROXY` mais pas `ALL_PROXY`. Avec seulement `HTTP_PROXY=…` posé, l'API GitLab sur `http://` passe par le proxy mais pas le clone. Avec seulement `ALL_PROXY=socks5://…`, c'est l'inverse : le clone passe par le proxy, aucun client Go. C'est le comportement de libcurl, pas du code DevDesk.
5. **Les noms `*.localhost` partent au proxy.** Go n'exempte que `localhost` exact. Un registre `foo.localhost:5000`, que `internal/oci` traite comme local (`isLocalURL`), est envoyé au proxy sauf si NO_PROXY le couvre.
6. **Les pulls ne passent pas par l'environnement de DevDesk.** Avec Docker, c'est le démon qui tire, selon sa propre config proxy (non vérifiable dans le code).
7. **Rien n'est documenté ni montré à l'utilisateur.** Aucune doc ne dit que DevDesk suit HTTP(S)_PROXY et NO_PROXY, que ALL_PROXY n'est pas lue, ni que les variables sont lues une fois au démarrage. Aucun écran n'indique le proxy actif. Il n'y a pas de test de contrat du type « chaque client de production garde `ProxyFromEnvironment` » : un futur `&http.Transport{…}` sans `Proxy`, comme celui de `netcheck`, passerait sans alerte.

### Recommandation

Une story me paraît justifiée, d'effort M. C'est d'abord une question de cohérence et de documentation ; il n'y a pas de bug bloquant sur les chemins principaux. Périmètre proposé :

- **a. Un seul point d'entrée.** Un transport partagé ou une fonction `Proxy` commune pour les clients de DevDesk. Plus un test de garde, sur le modèle des scans de source existants : il échoue si un `http.Transport` de production hors `nexusbench` et `forward` n'a pas `Proxy` (allowlist documentée).
- **b. `netcheck` honnête.** Il faut choisir entre :
  - garder le direct et ajouter une ligne « proxy configuré pour cette cible : X (ou exclu par NO_PROXY) » ;
  - ou faire aussi un HEAD par le proxy.

  C'est un choix produit à poser à l'utilisateur. Je recommande la première option, plus une ligne « via proxy » quand le direct échoue.
- **c. Moniteur `ssl` aligné** sur le moniteur `http` (CONNECT par le proxy), ou au moins une indication qu'il est direct.
- **d. Scanners en conteneur.** Transmettre `-e HTTP_PROXY -e HTTPS_PROXY -e NO_PROXY` (et les formes en minuscules) quand elles sont posées, avec un avertissement quand le proxy est en bouclage. À trancher : est-ce que DevDesk doit le faire, ou laisser `~/.docker/config.json` s'en charger ?
- **e. Documentation** (`docs/architecture/network.md`, plus une section utilisateur) :
  - les variables lues, la priorité des majuscules, la lecture unique au démarrage ;
  - ALL_PROXY non lue (mettre un SOCKS dans HTTPS_PROXY) ;
  - les CIDR de NO_PROXY qui ne visent que les IP littérales ;
  - `*.localhost` ;
  - l'écart avec git et libcurl ;
  - les pulls faits par le démon.

Je déconseille un réglage de proxy dans la config YAML de contexte tant qu'il n'y a pas de besoin exprimé. Il ferait double emploi avec l'environnement, et la garde SSRF de D156 devrait alors être revue.

**Non vérifiable dans le code :**
- le comportement proxy du démon Docker et de podman (pull, login, injection dans les conteneurs) ;
- la manière dont Trivy, cosign et plumber traitent eux-mêmes le proxy, une fois l'environnement reçu ;
- le support de `git archive --remote` en http(s) côté forges.

lastPrompt: demande à l'architect si devdesk respecte les variables http_proxy, https_proxy, no_proxy

content.text:
Oui pour presque tous les appels HTTP que DevDesk fait lui-même, mais par défaut et non par conception. Il n'a aucun réglage de proxy à lui (ni clé YAML, ni option, ni doc utilisateur) : ses clients Go passent par `http.ProxyFromEnvironment`, comme les sous-processus (`git`, `docker`, `trivy`) qui héritent de l'environnement. Cette analyse de l'`architect` est faite sur `main` (`9f878a2a`), en lecture seule.

## Ce que fait Go
- `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY` et `NO_PROXY` sont lues en majuscules comme en minuscules, la majuscule l'emporte.
- L'environnement est lu **une seule fois par processus** : un changement de contexte ne le relit pas.
- `NO_PROXY` accepte noms, suffixes, `*`, IP, CIDR et `hôte:port`. Un CIDR ne s'applique qu'à une IP littérale dans l'URL, jamais à un nom résolu.
- `ALL_PROXY` est **ignorée** par tous les clients Go. Pour un SOCKS, il faut le mettre dans `HTTPS_PROXY` (schémas `socks5` et `socks5h` acceptés).
- `localhost` exact et les IP de bouclage ne passent jamais par le proxy, mais un nom en `*.localhost` si.

## Qui respecte l'environnement
- **Oui :**
  - registres OCI, y compris les blobs de templates, avec une garde anti-SSRF qui sait autoriser le proxy ;
  - recherche d'images et colonne Update ;
  - API de gestion Nexus ;
  - checks de statut HTTP/HTTPS ;
  - API GitLab et GitHub ;
  - les sous-processus `git`, `docker`, `podman`, `trivy`, `gitleaks`, `cosign` installés comme binaires.
- **Non, volontairement :**
  - les forwards locaux ;
  - `nexusbench`, qui retire aussi les variables de proxy pour `skopeo`.
- **Non, sans que rien ne le signale :**
  - le HEAD HTTP des Diagnostics (`netcheck`, `env.go:306`) ;
  - le check SSL des moniteurs de statut, qui part en direct.
- **Non applicable :** DNS, ICMP, TCP brut, `nettrace`, MCP (serveur en écoute seulement).

## Les trous
1. **Diagnostics :** derrière un proxy obligatoire, l'écran conclut « injoignable » alors que les autres clients passent. Rien n'indique qu'un proxy est configuré.
2. **Moniteurs de statut :** un moniteur `http` passe par le proxy, un moniteur `ssl` sur le même hôte part en direct. L'un peut être vert et l'autre en erreur.
3. **Scanners lancés en conteneur :** Trivy et cosign ne reçoivent pas les variables de proxy de DevDesk. La CLI Docker n'injecte que `~/.docker/config.json`, podman transmet celles de l'hôte, et un proxy sur 127.0.0.1 n'est pas joignable depuis un conteneur en réseau bridge.
4. **Écart Go / git :** libcurl ignore `HTTP_PROXY` en majuscules pour les URL `http://` et lit `ALL_PROXY`. Avec seulement `HTTP_PROXY`, l'API GitLab passe par le proxy mais pas le clone, et avec seulement `ALL_PROXY` c'est l'inverse.
5. **`*.localhost` :** un registre `foo.localhost:5000`, que `internal/oci` traite comme local, part au proxy sauf si `NO_PROXY` le couvre.
6. **Pulls :** avec Docker, c'est le démon qui tire, avec sa propre config proxy, que le code ne permet pas de vérifier.
7. **Aucune documentation ni test de contrat :** un futur `&http.Transport{…}` sans `Proxy` passerait sans alerte.

## Garde anti-SSRF et `NO_PROXY`
Quand un proxy est choisi, la garde autorise son `ip:port`, donc un proxy local comme cntlm sur 127.0.0.1 continue de marcher. Une cible exclue par `NO_PROXY` part en direct et la garde s'applique à son IP. Le risque résiduel accepté (4) de D156 reste valable : une fois un proxy vu, son `ip:port` est autorisé pour toute connexion du transport.

## Non vérifiable dans le code
Le comportement proxy du démon Docker et de podman, la façon dont Trivy, cosign et plumber traitent eux-mêmes le proxy, et le support de `git archive --remote` en http(s).

## Recommandation de l'architect
Une story d'effort M, centrée sur la cohérence et la documentation (aucun bug bloquant sur les chemins principaux) :
- un point d'entrée commun pour le proxy, avec un test de garde qui échoue sur un `http.Transport` de production sans `Proxy` (liste d'exceptions documentée) ;
- Diagnostics et moniteur SSL : afficher le proxy configuré, ou passer par lui ;
- scanners en conteneur : transmettre les variables ;
- une section de documentation sur tout ce qui précède.

Il déconseille un réglage de proxy dans la config YAML tant qu'aucun besoin n'est exprimé, car il ferait double emploi avec l'environnement.

Deux points sont à ta décision avant d'écrire la story :
- **Diagnostics :** garder le direct avec une ligne « proxy configuré pour cette cible », ou faire aussi un HEAD par le proxy. L'`architect` recommande la première option.
- **Scanners en conteneur :** DevDesk transmet-il lui-même les variables, ou laisse-t-on `~/.docker/config.json` s'en charger ?

Veux-tu que le `pm` rédige cette story dans Plane ? Je ne la crée pas sans ton accord.

content.text:
Le `pm` crée la story dans Plane (en Backlog). Il vérifie d'abord qu'il n'y a pas de doublon. Je n'ai pas encore son résultat. Ci-dessous, l'explication de la position de l'`architect` sur les Diagnostics.

## Ton symptôme : SSL en erreur, HTTP qui passe
C'est le trou n° 2 de l'analyse. Le check HTTP/HTTPS des moniteurs passe par le proxy de l'environnement. Le check SSL, lui, ouvre une connexion TLS directe (`tls.DialWithDialer`, `internal/status/tls_dial.go:27`). Si ta machine ne peut sortir que par un proxy, le second échoue alors que le premier réussit. Cela colle avec ce que tu as vu, mais je n'ai rien vérifié sur ta machine. Les moniteurs et les Diagnostics sont deux écrans différents.

## Ce que l'`architect` a dit des Diagnostics
Ce n'est pas une décision tranchée : il l'a présenté comme un choix produit, c'est-à-dire à toi, avec une recommandation. Le constat de départ est que le HEAD HTTP des Diagnostics n'utilise pas le proxy (`netcheck/env.go:306`) et dépend d'une étape de connexion TCP directe. Derrière un proxy obligatoire, l'écran conclut donc « injoignable » alors que les autres clients de DevDesk passent, et rien n'indique qu'un proxy existe.

Il propose deux options :
1. **Garder le direct et l'expliquer (sa recommandation).** Les Diagnostics continuent de tester ce que la machine atteint directement. Ils ajoutent une ligne « proxy configuré pour cette cible : X » (ou « exclu par `NO_PROXY` »), plus une ligne « via proxy » quand le direct échoue.
2. **Faire aussi un HEAD par le proxy.**

Voici pourquoi la première me paraît cohérente avec ce qu'il a relevé. C'est mon raisonnement, il ne l'a pas écrit tel quel. Les Diagnostics enchaînent DNS, route, ICMP, TCP puis TLS, qui testent tous le chemin direct. Un HEAD passé par le proxy réussirait même quand l'étape TCP directe échoue, et l'écran se contredirait. Le garder direct reste fidèle à ce que les étapes mesurent, à condition de dire qu'un proxy existe.

## Suite
La story contiendra ces trois questions ouvertes, sans les trancher : Diagnostics direct avec indication ou HEAD par le proxy ; scanners en conteneur ; moniteur SSL via le proxy ou direct avec indication. Je te donne son identifiant, sa priorité et son effort dès que le `pm` a fini.
